title: tenant-slo-windowing-and-ephemeral-fallbacks-for-soft-degradation
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: During recent regional surges we observed tenant-level SLO violations triggering aggressive global circuit flips and mass eviction of low-priority requests. That behavior caused unnecessary cold-path rebuilds and DLL cache churn for tenants that were transiently hot in a small window. This PR implements a tenant-aware SLO windowing mechanism plus an ephemeral local fallback circuit that lets tenants degrade softly for short windows without affecting global circuit state.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a sliding tenant SLO window allocator (configurable window length and weight decay), a short-lived "ephemeral" local fallback circuit that can be raised/lowered per tenant-region for a configured grace period, and a prioritized token drain that preserves high-importance tokens (system, admin, and paid-priority) while shedding best-effort traffic. Also wires metrics, tracing, rollout flags, and an emergency hotfix toggle.

Key benefits and rationale: 1) Limits blast radius of transient spikes by keeping global circuits stable; 2) Enables soft degradation for tenants experiencing micro-surges without impacting sibling tenants; 3) Reduces cold-cache rewarm costs by avoiding full-eviction; 4) Gives product teams control via tenant-level knobs and short automatic decay.

Design notes: - Tenant SLO windows are tracked per (tenant, region, model_variant) and aggregate into a single moving-average score used by the SLO enforcer. The allocator uses a decayed sum with configurable half-life to avoid overreacting to single anomalies. - Ephemeral fallback circuit is a separate state machine with a short TTL (default 45s) and exponential backoff; it only controls soft-shed actions (priority-based token dropping and low-quality model variant routing). It does not flip global region circuit state. - Token prioritization: tokens are annotated at ingress; drain respects token classes (system>paid>free). Low-class tokens are dropped probabilistically with a ramp based on measured token pressure. - Rollout strategy: feature gated behind runtime flag slo.tenant_windowing; default off for 24-hour canary on selected tenants, then staged ramp.

Checklist: - [x] Implement window allocator and state persistence (- compact protobuf snapshot) - [x] Implement ephemeral circuit state machine and TTL-based decay - [x] Implement token prioritization and draining hooks in the request router - [x] Add metrics and tracing spans (tenant.window_score, tenant.ephemeral_state, token.drop_rate) - [x] Add configuration knobs and runtime feature gate - [x] Unit tests for allocator and circuit transitions - [x] Integration test with synthetic surge harness - [x] Docs and runbook updates - [x] Canary rollout and monitoring dashboard prepared

Backward compatibility and safety: Behavior is opt-in. Default runtime flag is off; when on we exercise only soft-shed paths. No breaking API changes. Config values have sensible conservative defaults to minimize false positives.

Performance: Local microbenchmarks show the allocator adds ~0.3% CPU and <1ms p90 request decision latency on our canary nodes. In synthetic surge tests we reduced global circuit flips by 78% and cache rewarm-related 95th latency by 22%.

Files changed (high level): see files_changed list for full paths. Key files include the SLO allocator core, ephemeral circuit manager, router draining hook, protobuf snapshots, runtime flags, tests, and docs.

Rollout plan and monitoring: - Stage 0: Internal canary (4 nodes) on dev cluster with slo.tenant_windowing=true for test tenants for 24h. - Stage 1: 10% tenant population in us-west for 48h with tight dashboards. - Stage 2: 50% ramp with automated abort if token drop_rate > 2.5% or tenant.window_score false-positive spikes > 3x baseline. Emergency toggle slo.disable_ephemeral=true to disable immediately.

Related work: complements ENG-4210 (regional soft-failover), refactors parts of ENG-4122 (per-tenant quotas). Supports SUP-1182 incident mitigation playbook.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of circuit transitions, serialization of allocator state across restarts, and ensuring drain preserves high-priority token semantics. The hotfix toggle path is intentionally minimal and covered by e2e.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approving reviews and a green CI run.

review_comments: Julian Park: Can we ensure allocator snapshots are written atomically to avoid partial restores? (see comment inline about temporary file rename) - Asha: Yes, using atomic tempfile+rename, added tests.

Leah Moreno: The token drain probabilities need a guard to avoid starving paid tokens under extreme noise. Suggest adding min_preserve for paid tokens. - Asha: Added min_preserve=0.98 for paid and system tokens; config default in flags.toml.
Samir Iqbal: CI flake on first run due to test harness timeout; reran and passed. Also suggested clearer dashboard alerts—updated.
Ops (post-merge): Confirmed canary tenants behaved as expected over 36h with no global flips.
release_notes: Introduces opt-in tenant SLO windowing and ephemeral local fallbacks to enable soft degradation during short tenant surges. Feature is behind runtime flag slo.tenant_windowing and includes a hotfix toggle slo.disable_ephemeral. Reduces global circuit flips and cache rewarm costs. See docs/ops/tenant_slo_windowing.md for runbook and config.
